title: How to (Accidentally) Spot an International Student in Baku. Tip #1
body: He came to Baku for MBBS and he has now explained why to roughly four hundred people. Cheaper than a private seat back home, English medium, recognised, and one uncle who knew a consultant. Ask how many students from his city are in the same building. The answer is never fewer than six. It's a sealed deal if he found the flat through a WhatsApp group before he ever landed.
caption:
Tip #1 😭 MBBS in Baku is a whole personality.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot an International Student in Baku. Tip #2
body: Watch the food situation, because it is the whole first year. He cooks. Not as a hobby, as survival, because month two is when the local food stops being an adventure. There is a rice cooker. There is a spice box brought from home in a suitcase that had a weight limit. There is one shop he has found that stocks the right lentils and he guards the location. It's a sealed deal if a relative has shipped him masala by cargo.
caption:
Tip #2 😭 MBBS in Baku is a whole personality.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot an International Student in Baku. Tip #3
body: Ask about the winter. He arrived in September thinking he understood cold. He did not. The Baku wind is not cold, it is personal, and it comes off the Caspian sideways. By January he owns a coat that would be absurd at home and is exactly correct here. It's a sealed deal if his first winter photo is him in three layers looking genuinely betrayed.
caption:
Tip #3 😭 MBBS in Baku is a whole personality.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot an International Student in Baku. Tip #4
body: Check the language situation. Six words of Azerbaijani, four of Russian, and a phone permanently on translate. He can order food, name body parts in Latin, and argue about rent, and that is the entire vocabulary. The patients speak neither Latin nor English. Clinical years are where this becomes a real problem and nobody warned him. It's a sealed deal if he has ever done a whole consultation through a classmate acting as interpreter.
caption:
Tip #4 😭 MBBS in Baku is a whole personality.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot an International Student in Baku. Tip #5
body: Ask where he lives. Yasamal, Nizami, or near the university, three or four to a flat, one landlord who communicates only through voice notes. The rent went up because everyone's rent went up. There is a group chat for the building. It's a sealed deal if he can tell you the exact bus or metro route to the anatomy block and the time it takes at each hour of the day.
caption:
Tip #5 😭 MBBS in Baku is a whole personality.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot an International Student in Baku. Tip #6
body: Watch what happens in summer. He goes home for two months and becomes a minor celebrity, the one studying abroad, and he does not correct anyone's assumptions about how glamorous it is. Then he comes back with a suitcase that is sixty percent food. It's a sealed deal if his mother has ever asked, seriously, whether they have vegetables in Azerbaijan.
caption:
Tip #6 😭 MBBS in Baku is a whole personality.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot an International Student in Baku. Tip #7
body: Ask about the exam back home, because that is the real finish line. FMGE, NEXT, the licensing exam, whatever it's called this year, and it hangs over all six years. He is not studying to be a doctor in Baku. He is studying to pass a test in another country. It's a sealed deal if he knows the pass rate percentage by heart and it comes up in casual conversation.
caption:
